open_world_validation.finding: multi-instance consensus boundary stress generalizes strongly across source families, but no single stress family covers every near-OOD direction; naive multi-scale spreading hurts, while random smooth virtual adversaries give a modest aggregate gain and still leave a blind direction.

depth_fusion.finding: with independent positive-affine output charts aligned by two anchors per used plugin, 0.6/0.4 interpolation tracks the independent-target fused program far better than hard primary routing or raw private-chart mixing.

design_updates: Gauge-aware fusion must depend on residual gauge group plus cross-plugin chart coupling/scope.
Open-world validation should be a portfolio/capability layer rather than one universal stress heuristic.
Persistent multi-instance agreement is useful both for routing uncertainty and for selecting stress queries that avoid instance-noise regions.
A grounded affine chart gives a concrete regime where neural interpolative fusion is identifiable and measurably distinct from routing.
next: Represent validation capabilities explicitly and actively select among them based on which residual alternatives they can falsify.
Integrate source routing, private-input gauge fixing, output chart alignment, and depth fusion in one program-level experiment.
Replace finite D4 private-input family with continuous learned proposals plus grounding fallback.
Test an unrelated held-out environment/model family without changing V2 core.
